=== [DR1] ===
CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# CHALLENGER, ROUND 1: Christ had a father of the flesh, Joseph, of the house of David

**Position.** The KJV names one man as the child's father: Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David." It requires a seed "according to the flesh" that came "out of the loins" of David. It reckons Jesus "of Juda" by the house of the fathers. "Of the Holy Ghost" marks where the child comes from in the covenant. It does not name a begetter of flesh. I hold every row the defender quoted, as written, and show how each fits.

---

## C1. The promise requires seed out of a man's body, according to the flesh

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
**[L2]** In Romans 1:3, *spermatos* (G4690, "seed, offspring") is joined to *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh"). In Acts 2:30, *osphys* (G3751, "loin, procreative power") is the same word used in Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." The loins in these rows are a father's loins.
**[L3]** Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." The margin reads "body: Heb. belly." Hebrews 2:14 says "he also himself likewise took part of the same," that is, of flesh and blood. Hebrews 2:16 carries the margin "Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold."
**[L4]** These rows set Christ's flesh as seed out of David's bowels and loins (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30), and the loins-word belongs to the father (Hebrews 7:10, *osphys*). Romans 1:3 gives *spermatos ... kata sarka*. So the flesh came down a line of fathers. The line the text names reaches "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).

## C2. Jesus is reckoned "of Juda" by the house of the fathers

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
**[L3]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
**[L2]** "By the house of their fathers" is *bayith* (H1004, "house, family") with *'ab* (H1, "father").
**[L3]** Ezra 2:62 shows what happened to men reckoned through a wife's house. Those "called after their name" (Ezra 2:61, the house of Barzillai's daughters) "sought their register ... but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
**[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 calls Jesus' descent from Juda "evident" (*prodēlon*, "plain beforehand"). The law reckons pedigree by the father's house (Numbers 1:18, *bayith* and *'ab*). The text gives the house of one man: "Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27) and "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). So Jesus' descent from Juda is evident through Joseph.

## C3. The father is named by Mary, the narrator, the town and a disciple

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." This is Mary speaking.
**[L3]** Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year." This is the narrator. Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled." John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." This is Philip, a disciple.
**[L2]** In Luke 2:41 the word is *goneis* (G1118, "parents, those who beget"), from the root of *ginomai* ("to become, be born").
**[L4]** In Luke 2:48 Mary, the one the angel spoke to, calls Joseph *ho patēr sou* ("thy father"). The narrator calls the two of them *goneis* ("parents"). The father is named by the witness closest to the conception.

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES (the defender's chain, link by link)

The defender's links each take as given a fact that the rows they quote do not supply. The witnesses below carry the layers.

**1. LINK D1.** Defender's words: "with a human source only in Mary."
ASSUMES: the Davidic flesh of Romans 1:3 came to the child through Mary's house.
ROWS GIVE: Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"; Luke 2:4, "he was of the house and lineage of David"; Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth"; Luke 1:5, "his wife was of the daughters of Aaron."
PRESSED WITH: Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30; Hebrews 7:10.
- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690, "seed") and *osphys* (G3751, "loins," in Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:10, "in the loins of his father").
- **[L4]** The flesh-seed comes from a father's loins. The house of David is given to Joseph, while Mary's cousin is "of the daughters of Aaron." So the defender's "only in Mary" routes David's seed through a house the rows give to the husband.
- **On "born of thee" (ek sou, "out of thee," Luke 1:35):** Matthew uses *ek* ("out of") for the mother alongside a named father. Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:5: "Booz begat Obed of Ruth." *Ek* with the mother is the genealogy's own marker for the mother. It fits a father who begat.

**2. LINK D2.** Defender's words: "a conception through an ordinary husband would be no sign."
ASSUMES: a child conceived through a husband falls outside Isaiah's sign.
ROWS GIVE: Isaiah 8:3, "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son" (margin: "went: Heb. approached"); Isaiah 8:18, "Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel."
PRESSED WITH: Isaiah 7:16; Isaiah 8:4; Isaiah 8:8.
- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:4: "before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother." Isaiah 8:8: "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *'ot* (H226, "sign") is the word of Isaiah 7:14. It returns in the plural in Isaiah 8:18, of children the prophet fathered.
- **[L4]** Isaiah 7:16 dates the sign to the two kings of Ahaz's day. Isaiah 8:3-4 gives the sign-child's conception after "I went unto the prophetess," and 8:4 gives that child a "father." Isaiah 8:18 names the prophet's own children as signs. So in Isaiah's own chapters, a sign-child comes through a husband.
- **How Matthew 1:22 fits:** Matthew applies the row the same way he applies Hosea 11:1 at Matthew 2:15: "Out of Egypt have I called my son." That row was first spoken of Israel: "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt" (Hosea 11:1). Fulfilment in Matthew fills a row whose first subject stood in its own day. Matthew and Isaiah stand together.

**3. LINK D3.** Defender's words: "the genealogy deliberately declines to call Joseph the begetter of Jesus."
ASSUMES: the feminine *ex hēs* ("out of whom") at Matthew 1:16 removes the husband from the begetting.
ROWS GIVE: Matthew 1:16, "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus"; Matthew 1:3, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar"; Matthew 1:5, "Booz begat Obed of Ruth."
PRESSED WITH: Galatians 4:4; Job 14:1; Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13.
- **[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- **[L3]** Job 14:1: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days." Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias ... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L2]** *egennēthē* ("was born," passive) with *ek* ("out of") the woman is the "born of a woman" phrase. *ek* with the mother is Matthew's marker at 1:3 and 1:5, beside fathers who begat.
- **[L4]** "Born of a woman" is said of John, whose father is named (Luke 1:13). *ek* with the mother stands beside a begetting father in Matthew 1:3 and 1:5. So the form at 1:16 names the mother in the genealogy's own way. The same verse calls Joseph *andra* ("husband").

**4. LINK D4.** Defender's words: "A man who knew himself the father would have had no cause for the intended divorce." Also: "The word marks a popular opinion, not a fact."
ASSUMES: Joseph's purpose at Matthew 1:19 rested on knowing the child was another man's, and *enomizeto* marks a mistaken opinion.
ROWS GIVE: Matthew 1:19, "being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example"; Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made"; Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:20; Matthew 1:21; Luke 1:32; 1 Chronicles 28:6.

**The meaning the defender claims for Matthew 1:19 is that Joseph's cause was knowing the child was not his.** Here is how the row fits my link:
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19 states Joseph's intent and gives two grounds. One is *dikaios ōn* ("being just"). The other is *mē thelōn ... paradeigmatisai* ("not willing to make a public example"). *Eboulēthē* ("was minded") is a verb of intent.
- **[L3]** The angel's answer is to his fear: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20, margin "conceived: Gr. begotten"). Then: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21). Naming is the father's act. Luke 1:62 reads: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."
- **[L4]** The angel addresses Joseph as "son of David." It grounds "fear not to take" in the child's covenant origin. It gives Joseph the father's act of naming. So the angel answers a just man's fear by confirming him as the Davidic father of the promised seed, the one of whom God said, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14). That fits my link.

**On *enomizeto* ("was supposed, was reckoned by usage"), G3543:**
- **[L2]** The word comes from *nomos* ("law, custom"): "to do by law (usage)."
- **[L3]** The same form, *enomizeto*, appears at Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." There it marks what was customary and was in fact so.
- **[L4]** Luke's reckoning "son of Joseph" (Luke 3:23) stands beside Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) and the law's reckoning "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).

**On Luke 2:49:**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Two fathers stand in one verse.
- **[L3]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." David's begotten son and God's covenant son are the same person in one verse.
- **[L4]** "My Father's business" (Luke 2:49) is the covenant title. "Thy father" (Luke 2:48) is the father of the flesh. Both stand, as they stand together for Solomon.

**5. LINK D5.** Defender's words: "So the question "biological father?" has no human answer in the record."
ASSUMES: the child's flesh came apart from a father's seed.
ROWS GIVE: Luke 24:39, "a spirit hath not flesh and bones"; Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh"; Hebrews 2:17, "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren."
PRESSED WITH: John 3:6; Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34; 1 John 5:1.
- **[L1]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- **[L3]** Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me." This uses the *eperchomai* ("come upon") of Luke 1:35, said of the apostles. Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." This uses the *episkiazō* ("overshadow") of Luke 1:35, said of the transfiguration cloud.
- **[L2]** *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("of holy spirit," Matthew 1:20) has the same *ek* with *gennaō* that 1 John 5:1 says of believers: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him."
- **[L4]** The defender's own Luke 24:39 puts flesh and bones outside a spirit, and John 3:6 keeps flesh-born and Spirit-born as two. So the flesh "made like unto his brethren" (Hebrews 2:17) came as Romans 1:3 gives it: seed of David according to the flesh. "Of the Holy Ghost" is the covenant-origin phrase that 1 John 5:1 uses of the begotten of God.
- **On Luke 1:35's *dio kai* ("therefore also"):** It connects back to v.32, not forward to divine paternity of the flesh. The title "Son of the Highest" and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.

**On the timing rows the defender pressed (Matthew 1:18, Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:25), held as written:**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." Matthew sets what "came together" means by what follows: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24).
- **[L3]** The law names that same step: "what man is there that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" (Deuteronomy 20:7). Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man," uses *ginōskō* ("know") in the present indicative: her state when the angel spoke. The angel's "thou shalt conceive" (Luke 1:31) is future.
- **[L4]** The seed rows of C1 require seed out of a man's loins. The canon's stated means of begetting is "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20), and the law's "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24). "Knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the time after the taking. So, on these rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

**6. LINK D6 (keystone).** Defender's words: "Christ had no biological father."
ASSUMES: links D1 to D5 stand.
ROWS GIVE: Hebrews 7:14, "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"; Numbers 1:2, "by the house of their fathers ... every male by their polls"; Luke 2:48, "thy father and I."
PRESSED WITH: Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30; 2 Samuel 7:12; Luke 2:4.
- **[L4]** Each supporting link is pressed above. The keystone rests on them. The seed rows (C1), the reckoning rows (C2) and the named-father rows (C3) give a father of the flesh, Joseph, of the house and lineage of David.

---

**CHALLENGE TO THE DEFENDER:** Hebrews 7:14 reads: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The law reckons by "the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18). Show, from quoted rows, the father's house by which this descent is evident.

=== [DR2] ===
CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 2, CLOSING AND PREMISE LIST

# CHALLENGER, ROUND 2 OF CHALLENGE

The defender has granted three rows: Joseph is "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27; Luke 2:4), Mary calls Joseph "thy father" (Luke 2:48), and "born of a woman" is said of men who had fathers (Job 14:1; Matthew 11:11). Each grant carries the case to Joseph. Below I meet every press in Round 2 by showing how it fits my link.

---

## A. The house by which "sprang out of Juda" is evident

**The defender's answer splits the child into two houses.** The register runs through Joseph, which is granted. The flesh runs "by the house of Mary's father," Heli.

**[L1]** Ezra 2:59: "but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [seed: or, pedigree]"
**[L2]** *'ab* (H1, "father") with *bayith* (H1004, "house, family"). The standing of a lay Israelite is shown by "their father's house" and their seed (margin: "pedigree").
**[L3]** Ezra 2:61-62: the man "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". Of that house: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood. [were they...: Heb. they were polluted from the priesthood]"
**[L4]** The defender's own example of a man "called after" his wife's father's name is the case the register put out. Ezra 2:59 applies the father's-house rule to Israel at large ("whether they were of Israel"), not to priests only. Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers," is the law Hebrews 7:14 answers to. The row Luke 3:23 sets beside Heli is "the son of Joseph." The house the rows give is Joseph's: "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

## B. Jeremiah 22:30, answered by the LORD himself

**[L1]** Jeremiah 22:24: "though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence."
**[L3]** Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." 1 Chronicles 3:17: "And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, [Salathiel: Heb. Shealtiel]". Jeremiah 18:8: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them."
**[L2]** *chotham*, "signet," is the same seal-word in both rows. The LORD plucks it from Coniah, and the LORD sets it on Coniah's grandson.
**[L4]** The LORD himself puts the signet back on Shealtiel's son, under the rule he states in Jeremiah 18:8. Matthew 1:12 follows that line: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." The defender's Nathan route also carries the same two names: "which was [the son] of Zorobabel, which was [the son] of Salathiel, which was [the son] of Neri" (Luke 3:27). The Heli route brings the defender to the same names it was built to avoid. The curse row fits a Davidic father through Joseph, with the LORD's own reversal written beside it.

## C. Loins down a line: a line of fathers

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:9-10: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham. For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
**[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren". Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham".
**[L2]** *osphys* (G3751, "loin; procreative power") and *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate, properly of the father").
**[L4]** The defender is right that the loins-phrase reaches down several generations. The generations it reaches through are begettings: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, then Levi among "Judas and his brethren." So Acts 2:30, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh," reaches Christ down a line of fathers, and the father the rows name at the end is "Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27).

## D. "Her seed" and "made of a woman"

**[L1]** Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. [Seth: Heb. Sheth: that is Appointed, or, Put]"
**[L2]** *zera'* ("seed, posterity") is the word of Genesis 3:15, "her seed." *sperma* (G4690) in Romans 1:3 is glossed "seed (including the male 'sperm')."
**[L3]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Romans 1:4: "And declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]"
**[L4]** Eve's "seed" in Genesis 4:25 is a son whose father "knew his wife." A woman's seed therefore stands beside a named father.
- The defender granted that "made of a woman" is said of men with fathers.
- The defender then rested "the seed of David ... through the woman" on that same phrase and verb ("the same verb, the same *ek*").
- A granted row cannot then carry the opposite load.

Romans 1:3-4 joins two things. The flesh is "seed of David according to the flesh." The title is "declared ... by the resurrection."

## E. Matthew 1:19-20: the means of the press, met

The defender says: "A husband who knew himself the source would have no such fear and no need for that word."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
**[L3]** Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
**[L2]** *mē phobou ... gar* ("fear not ... for") stands in both rows. *kaleō* (G2564, "to call, name") is given to the man in both rows: "thou shalt call his name."
**[L4]** The angel's address to Zacharias has the same form as Matthew 1:20-21:
- "fear not";
- "for" with a word about the child;
- "thy wife";
- "thou shalt call his name."

Zacharias is the father, and he too is given "fear not" and a word about his son. So "fear not ... for" is the form in which the text addresses a father, and Joseph's fear is answered the same way. Matthew 1:19 gives Joseph's grounds as *dikaios* ("just") and "not willing to make her a publick example." The angel answers a just man's fear about taking her by showing him the child's covenant origin and destiny, the son of whom God says, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14). That fits my link.

## F. *enomizeto*, "supposed"

**[L1]** Luke 2:44: "But they, supposing him to have been in the company." The ones supposing are Joseph and Mary.
**[L3]** Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made" uses the same form, *enomizeto*, of a custom that was true. [sabbath: Gr. sabbath day]
**[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543): "from νόμος; properly, to do by law (usage)."
**[L4]** The word's verdict comes from its context. In Luke, that context is the narrator's "his parents" (*goneis*, Luke 2:41), "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:33), and Mary's "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48). Luke 3:23 stands with these rows, as the reckoning by usage, the custom of the law.

## G. Luke 1:35 and Luke 2:49

**[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
**[L3]** Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me. [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]". Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."
**[L2]** *eperchomai* (G1904, "come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow") are said of the apostles and of the transfiguration cloud.

The dio kai ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.

**[L4]** The defender says Solomon's sonship rests on choice (*bachar*). Luke 1:32 gives the title and "his father David" in one verse, as 1 Chronicles 28:6 gives "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son." So "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49) and "thy father" (Luke 2:48) stand together as they stand for Solomon.

## H. The timing rows, read as one chain

**[L1]** Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife". This is said of the same betrothed damsel whom 22:23 calls "a virgin".
**[L3]** Deuteronomy 20:7: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife".
**[L2]** In Matthew 1:18, *synelthein* ("to come together") is set by what follows, her being taken into his house (Matthew 1:24). In Luke 1:34, *ginōskō* is present indicative, her state when the angel spoke. Luke 1:31's "thou shalt conceive" is future.
**[L4]** The law calls the betrothed both "a virgin" and "his neighbour's wife." So "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19) and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) name a marriage from the espousal. The seed rows require seed out of a man's loins (Acts 2:30). The canon's stated means of begetting is "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). "Knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the time after the taking. So, on these rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

## I. Isaiah 8, on the defender's own grant

**[L1]** Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. [went: Heb. approached]"
**[L3]** Isaiah 8:8: "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel. [stretching...: Heb. fulness of the breadth of thy land shall be the stretchings out of his wings]". Isaiah 8:18: "I and the children whom the LORD hath given me [are] for signs".
**[L4]** The defender grants, from Hosea 11:1 and Matthew 2:15, that a row has a first subject in its own day. In Isaiah's own day, Immanuel's land is overrun by Assyria (8:8). The sign-children are the prophet's own (8:18), and the sign-child is conceived after the prophet "approached" his wife (8:3).
